production_candidate_decision.basis: Seven completed valid comparison/qualification studies; retain the validated candidate.
production_candidate_decision.reason: Provider HTTP 402 prevents evaluating shorter variants; no promotion from invalid measurements.

counting_rule: One execution is one scheduled task × arm × repetition. Count each completed real observation once; categories, comparisons, follow-up API requests and offline fixtures add no executions. Tasks recur across studies; this is not a unique-task count. The 150 provider-402 executions count as attempted tests, not valid latency/quality comparisons.
excluded_runs: Offline fixtures, prepare-only experiments, rejected preparations and unrelated historical runs.
timing_scope: Actual in-process AdvisorSession selection including fresh frame validation, preparation, lazy first connection and all calls; one independent client per arm/repetition, first cold call retained. No warmup or result/index cache. Process imports, key-file read and freeze verification excluded.
instrumentation: Durable per-request wire/receipt writes and fsync are inside timing for every arm. Overhead was not subtracted or separately quantified; additional calls also carry this measurement overhead.
hussi_scope: Pinned published chooser with the same persistent HTTPS transport as a modified control; original confidence 0.8 and timeout 1.2 seconds. Whole product hooks and fallback models are not measured.
inference_limits: Synthetic tasks and fixed catalogs; selection latency, not full-agent task speed.
Only the 64-task independently authored study is labelled fresh holdout; earlier holdouts reused here are regression/comparison tasks.
Failed candidate variants and all their observed losses remain present. The entirely HTTP-402 cohort has no comparable speed or quality score.
Provider input tokens are response-reported observations, not independently verified billing or hidden backend identity.
Bootstrap intervals describe paired task variation in this fixed experiment, not deployment-wide uncertainty.
